name: isAvailable actually invoked somewhere vs never invoked at all
side_a: Award A1 whenever the response contains at least one invocation of isAvailable (on Account/this, with a string-intended argument) anywhere in the constructor — e.g., inside an if condition or a while loop test. Formatting wrappers (answer tags, code fences) and logic errors elsewhere do not matter.
side_b: Deduct A1 when the response never calls isAvailable at all — the constructor just assigns the requested name (or otherwise sets username) without ever testing availability; there is no call to find, so nothing can be credited no matter how well-formed the rest of the code is.

name: Availability is actually tested via isAvailable vs. requested name assigned unconditionally
side_a: no_deduct — the constructor invokes isAvailable(...) on a candidate name and only assigns username to a name that passed that test (either the original or a suffixed variant).
side_b: deduct — the constructor never calls isAvailable at all and assigns the requested name directly to username, so no availability logic exists.

name: Counter is actually advanced inside the loop body vs counter declared but never updated
side_a: Give the point (no_deduct) when a statement that advances the counter (e.g. `i++`) actually appears inside the loop body, so each repetition uses a new suffix value.
side_b: Deduct when the counter variable is only declared/initialized outside the loop and the loop body contains no increment (no `suffix++` or equivalent), leaving the counter frozen across iterations — merely having a counter variable plus a loop is not enough.

name: Some repeated-attempt structure with a counter exists vs no loop/counter at all
side_a: Give the point (no_deduct) when the answer contains some repetition structure that re-tests availability with a counter-derived name.
side_b: Deduct when the answer contains no loop and no counter whatsoever — it simply assigns the requested name — so there is nothing that could be incremented per attempt.

name: Tries the unmodified requestedName (guarded by isAvailable) before appending digits vs. never tests the bare name
side_a: No deduction if the code first calls isAvailable on the raw requestedName and assigns it unchanged when available, only falling through to the numbered-suffix search otherwise.
side_b: Deduct if the bare requestedName is never tested with isAvailable before assignment — either it is assigned outright with no check, or the search begins immediately at requestedName + digit so the unmodified name can never be chosen.

name: Numeric suffix search starts at 1 vs. starts at 0
side_a: No deduction if the appended counter is initialized to 1 so the first alternative tried is requestedName + 1.
side_b: Deduct if the counter starts at 0 (or any value other than 1), so the first alternative tried is requestedName + 0, violating the specified numbering.
